What does the AI Readiness Assessment deliver and what does it cost?

AI Readiness Assessment from Dave Willemstein shows organizations that are considering AI but have not chosen a direction yet what is realistic and what should happen first. The result is a readiness score across strategy, data, technology, people and governance, a gap analysis and a 90-day plan. The assessment takes 2-3 weeks for a fixed project fee, set out in the proposal, excluding VAT and travel expenses.
How long does the AI Readiness Assessment take?
2-3 weeks. In that period AI Readiness Assessment covers a document analysis, a data scan and 8-12 interviews, followed by scoring, prioritization and a closing session.
Is the price of the AI Readiness Assessment a fixed price?

Yes, for the whole organization: AI Readiness Assessment is priced as a fixed project fee, and the closing presentation to leadership or the board is included. For a single business unit or process domain, the investment is lower. All proposals are excluding VAT and travel expenses.
Source: Dave Willemstein's rates and typical timelines. Updated: October 2026.

Answers to what you are thinking now.
How much time will this take my team?+
Budget 45-60 minutes per person interviewed, plus two 90-minute sessions with the core group. I will not ask for more than that. Most of the work I do myself, based on documents, systems and data.
Do I get a scorecard or an opinion?+
Both, but the opinion is the product. A score without interpretation is a number without meaning. In the closing session I explain which score you can ignore and which one you should take seriously.
What if the outcome is that we are not ready yet?+
Then that is the most valuable outcome you can get for this price. You get a foundation plan instead of a use-case plan, and you avoid a failed initiative.
Can this be done for one department instead of the whole organization?+
Yes. For a single business unit or a specific process domain, the assessment typically takes two weeks and the investment is lower. We discuss that in the intake.
